Name: Duke Lung Cancer Screening (DLCS) Dataset
Comments: A reference dataset of annotated low-dose screening thoracic CT scans from a high-volume lung cancer screening center.  Intended for lung cancer risk stratification, radiomics analysis, and development of AI algorithms for lung nodule detection and classification. Includes Lung-RADS scores and, if applicable, timing and characteristics of future lung cancer diagnoses.

Imaging.Acquisition: Detailed acquisition parameters referenced in a prior study (13), but not provided in this article.
Imaging.Quality: Scans excluded if Lung-RADS 0, image or report data unavailable, or no nodules met annotation criteria (size ≥ 4 mm or any segmental/proximal airway nodule).

Composition.Number of instances: 2061 LDCT scans; 3187 annotated nodules. Publicly available subset: 1613 scans, 2487 nodules. Held-out test set: 448 scans.
Composition.Demographics: 1032 female, 1029 male patients; mean age 66.7 years ± 6.2 (SD).  Detailed demographics in Table 1 (not provided in article).
Composition.Disease Distribution: 7.5% (155 of 2061) of patients had later diagnoses of lung cancer.
Composition.Temporal: Data collected from January 1, 2015, through June 30, 2021. Minimum 1-year follow-up available for some patients.

Technical.Storage: De-identified data stored as Neuroimaging Informatics Technology Initiative (NIfTI) files. Annotations stored as .obj files (containing 8 coordinates representing a 3D bounding box).
Technical.Privacy: Data de-identified to remove protected health information (PHI). HIPAA compliant.
Technical.Validation: A held-out test set of 448 scans (21.7%) was withheld.
Technical.Benchmarking: The MONAI algorithm used for annotation had previously reported cross-validation sensitivities of 0.835 and 0.988 at different false positive rates (14).

Clinical.Application: Lung cancer screening workflow; lung cancer risk stratification; radiomics analysis; development of AI algorithms for lung nodule detection and classification.
Clinical.Impact: Potential to improve lung cancer screening and diagnosis through the development and validation of AI algorithms.
